clue.text: Going over again to see about surrender

parts.note: re is a short word meaning about or concerning
a capitulation is a surrender to an enemy

explanation.surface: Someone checks again on what happened at a surrender.
explanation.definitionFit: To recapitulate is to summarise or repeat the main points, going through them once more.

clue.text: Is up in arms about current affairs

parts.note: re is a short word meaning about or concerning
volts are units of electric potential, so things to do with electric current

explanation.surface: Someone is furious about the state of the news.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who revolts rebels, taking up arms against authority.

clue.text: Hap'orth of tar from a hawker?

parts.note: something worth a halfpenny is cheap
a jack, like a tar, is a sailor

explanation.surface: A halfpenny's worth of tar bought from a street seller, echoing the saying about spoiling the ship.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface recalls the proverb 'spoil the ship for a ha'porth of tar'. A halfpenny sailor is a cheap jack.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheapjack is a seller of cheap wares, a pedlar crying goods in the street.

clue.text: One step and set of three on the hoof

parts.note: pas is French for a step, especially in ballet
a tern is a set of three, as in a lottery or verse

explanation.surface: A dance step and a trio, as if describing a horse's gait.
explanation.definitionFit: The pastern is the part of a horse's foot between fetlock and hoof.

clue.text: Environs of Ilium, let's have tea on the way

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: T is the usual short form for tea
a road is a way

explanation.surface: A traveller near ancient Troy suggests stopping for tea along the road.
explanation.definitionFit: The Troad is the region round ancient Troy, also called Ilium, in north-west Asia Minor.

clue.text: His master was a regular Don Juan

definitions.text: His master was a regular Don Juan

parts.words: His master was a regular Don Juan
parts.note: the servant whose employer is Don Giovanni, the operatic Don Juan, here described as truly a seducer

explanation.definitionFit: Leporello is the manservant of Don Giovanni in Mozart's opera, and keeps the catalogue of his master's conquests.

clue.text: Camping girl hit on the head

definitions.text: Camping girl hit on the head

parts.words: Camping girl hit on the head
parts.note: the girl's name Peg plus a camping item, and that wooden item is struck on the head with a mallet

explanation.definitionFit: A tent-peg is the stake driven into the ground with blows to its top to hold a tent's ropes.

clue.text: Chose thus to do, pet

indicators.note: thus says the next words are arranged in this way, rearranging their letters

explanation.surface: Someone decided this was how to treat a darling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thus' signals rearranging DO and PET; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To opt is to choose, so opted is the past tense chose.

clue.text: Somewhere in France — not Ireland !

parts.note: a French city whose name, read in English, means the same as ire and so is a sort of land of ires

explanation.definitionFit: Angers is a city in western France on the Maine, whose name in English means rages.

clue.text: Opinions we back in force

indicators.note: in says one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: vis is Latin for force

indicators.note: back says the word we is turned round

explanation.surface: We hold our views firmly, defending them with force.
explanation.definitionFit: Views are opinions or points of view held by someone.

clue.text: Where to retire on a nest-egg ?

definitions.text: Where to retire on a nest-egg ?

parts.words: Where to retire on a nest-egg ?
parts.note: a Kent suburb that is also a breed of hen, which goes to roost on its egg

explanation.definitionFit: Orpington is a town on the edge of London in Kent and gives its name to a breed of domestic chicken.

clue.text: He does not depend on hearsay

definitions.text: He does not depend on hearsay

parts.words: He does not depend on hearsay
parts.note: someone who does not rely on what is heard, because they follow mouth movements instead

explanation.definitionFit: A lip-reader understands speech by watching the speaker's mouth, usually because of deafness.

clue.text: Father goes mottled red, father

parts.note: pa is a familiar word for father

indicators.note: mottled means blotched, so the letters of red are mixed up

explanation.walkthrough: 'mottled' shuffles RED into DRE; 'goes' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Padre is a title for a priest, especially a chaplain, addressed as Father.

clue.text: Church composer in the church glass, business ?

explanation.surface: A composer of church music tied up in the stained glass trade.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir John Stainer was a Victorian composer of church music; a stainer also colours glass, as for church windows.
explanation.definitionFit: John Stainer wrote church music such as The Crucifixion; a stainer is a worker who colours materials like glass.

clue.text: It's situated somewhere between S. and F.

definitions.text: It's situated somewhere between S. and F.

parts.words: It's situated somewhere between S. and F.
parts.note: a watch part whose lever moves on a scale marked S for slow and F for fast

explanation.definitionFit: The regulator in a clock or watch adjusts its rate, set between slow and fast marks.

clue.text: Runs from glances from the members

definitions.text: Runs from glances from the members

parts.words: Runs from glances from the members
parts.note: cricket runs scored when the ball glances off a batsman's limbs

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, leg byes are runs taken after the ball deflects off the batsman's body, not the bat.
explanation.definitionFit: Leg byes are extras in cricket, runs scored after the ball strikes the batsman's body.

clue.text: Such a thin drink!

parts.note: the drink is thin because its glass is long and narrow, a measure of beer

explanation.definitionFit: A yard of ale is beer drunk from a narrow trumpet-shaped glass about three feet long.

clue.text: Blackheath suggestion ?

parts.note: ink is black
ling is heather, a heath plant

explanation.surface: A hint coming from Blackheath, a district of south-east London.
explanation.definitionFit: An inkling is a slight hint or suggestion of something.

clue.text: Put the dean in his place!

definitions.text: Put the dean in his place!

parts.words: Put the dean in his place!
parts.note: a cathedral dean is given his formal seat, a stall in the choir

explanation.definitionFit: To instal, older spelling of install, originally meant to place a cleric in his stall, an official seat.

clue.text: I mulled, stirred, brightened

indicators.note: stirred, like a mulled drink, says the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: Someone warms and stirs spiced wine, and cheers up.
explanation.definitionFit: Illumed is a poetic word for lit up or illuminated.

clue.text: Not bothouse produce, nor stoneless

explanation.surface: A gardener describes fruit grown outdoors with its stones still in.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words, out crop is a crop grown outdoors, not in a hothouse; an outcrop of rock is certainly not without stones.
explanation.definitionFit: An outcrop is rock showing at the surface, and the split reading names a crop raised outside rather than under glass.

clue.text: Slow-motion defence

parts.note: a Roman shield formation named after the slowest animal, a tortoise

explanation.definitionFit: A testudo is the Roman tactic of overlapping shields, Latin for tortoise, advancing slowly under cover.

clue.text: Advances by choice

explanation.definitionFit: To prefer is to promote someone to office, and also to like one thing better than another.

clue.text: For sails and ropes

indicators.note: for here means changed into, giving another arrangement of the same letters

explanation.surface: Material used for a ship's sails and rigging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For' signals the anagram of SAILS; 'and' is a link. The definition is ropes, made from this fibre.
explanation.definitionFit: Sisal is the plant fibre twisted into ropes and twine.

clue.text: Battle between French banks

explanation.surface: A fight fought across a French river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Somme was a great battle of 1916, and a French river flowing between banks.

clue.text: So many poems have a musical quality that is attractive

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty, so many
odes are lyrical poems
tone is the quality of a musical sound

explanation.surface: Many poems sound lovely to the ear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'So many' is a stock way of giving a Roman numeral, here L for fifty; 'have' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Lodestone is naturally magnetic iron ore, which pulls iron towards it.

clue.text: "The — reed once more, Well pleased, I tune" (Thomson)

definitions.text: "The — reed once more, Well pleased, I tune" (Thomson)

parts.words: "The — reed once more, Well pleased, I tune" (Thomson)
parts.note: a line from James Thomson with an adjective missing before reed, meaning rustic or pastoral

explanation.definitionFit: Doric means rustic or pastoral, after the Greek dialect of shepherd poetry, so a shepherd's pipe is a Doric reed.

clue.text: Battle, one with bairns — to school with them !

parts.note: the Alma was an 1854 Crimean War battle
mater is Latin for mother, one with children; bairns is Scots for children

explanation.surface: A Scot remembers a battle and a mother of children, then sends them off to school.
explanation.definitionFit: Alma mater is the school or college someone attended.

clue.text: It's the custom to finish a banger

indicators.note: the finish of the word is its end, so its opening letters are dropped

parts.note: banger is British slang for a sausage

explanation.surface: Tradition says you must eat up your sausage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finish' keeps only the end of SAUSAGE, losing SA. A banger is a British sausage.
explanation.definitionFit: Usage is customary practice, the way things are habitually done.

clue.text: Masterman & Summers, figure consultants

parts.note: names that sound like a firm of advisers, really compilers of books of worked-out sums consulted for figures

explanation.definitionFit: Ready reckoners are books of precalculated tables consulted to find sums quickly.
